documents.text: How to print Support for PLA/PETG with Bambu Cool Plate SuperTack
documents.note: Linked from both wiki pages (SuperTack wiki "refer to this wiki"; plates wiki Further Reading); not cached, so not read for specs.

notes: Sizes per printer come from the SuperTack wiki "Compatible Models" table (350*320 mm H2D / H2S; 330*320 mm H2C / A2L; 256*256 mm X2D / P2S / P1 Series / X1 Series / A1); the plates wiki's general dimensions table gives the same rows. Stored as product.length/product.width per Printer Model option. They agree with the store page's "Usable Print Size" row.

Material: the page row "Specially Designed Coating / Spring Steel Plate" (part.material, verified) is repeated with its quote (same value and rank, so the merge keeps the page row unchanged); the wiki's "coating a spring steel sheet with SuperTack" says the same, so the coating name is curated as part.surface_treatment instead of rewording part.material.
Thickness: only the store page gives it ("Coating - 0.05mm / Steel Plate - 0.4mm"); left to the page row (unverified; its value_num 0.05 is the coating layer). No curated thickness.

Generations: the SuperTack wiki says the 256×256 mm plate exists as the original and the SuperTack Pro (updated QR code identification); the store page offers "Cool Plate SuperTack" options for X2D / P2S / A1 / P1 Series / X1 Series and "Cool Plate SuperTack Pro" options for A2L / H2C / H2S / H2D, and does not say which 256 mm generation it ships. No generation-specific spec or relation is written; the plate-detection advice is kept in the printer relations' notes and as the page's variant.note rows.

A1 mini: the SuperTack wiki's Installation Steps pictures include an "A1 mini" row, but its Compatible Models table, the plates wiki and the store page offer no A1 mini size, so no A1 mini relation is written.
Marketing prose not stored as numbers: "less than 20% adhesion loss after 300 prints" (test with PLA Basic on the A1) and the energy-saving claims.

Bed temperatures (PLA 45℃ on the store comparison table, 40 °C in the plates wiki; PETG 55–60 °C for the 2nd-generation plate, around 65 °C on the X/P series) have no registry key for a plate (print_settings.* applies to filament only); they are kept in the material relations' notes. Removal aid "heat the plate on the heatbed to 50°C" is a usage step on the page.
Glue: "SuperTack provides good adhesion without adhesive", so no requires relation is written.
The wiki video https://public-cdn.bblmw.com/wiki/accessory/Bambu-Cool-Plate-SuperTack-en.mp4 is on a host outside the document allow-list, so it is not listed as a document.

Packaging Size / Packaging Weight and Usable Print Size: the store table labels each segment by printer models ("X1C/P1P/P1S/A1/P2S/X2D", "H2D/H2S", "H2C/A2L"). Usable print size, a property of the plate, is written per Printer Model value; the packaging figures are written per plate-only variant (Printer Model × "Cool Plate SuperTack" or "Cool Plate SuperTack Pro"), because the "+ Mag-Alloy Scraper" bundles share the Printer Model values and have no figures of their own. The H2C/A2L plate (330*320 mm) ships in the same 393*380*15 mm box as the H2D/H2S plate, 0.46 kg against 0.48 kg, as published. No CBM is derived; no net weight of the plate is published.

Bundles: the "+ Mag-Alloy Scraper" options name a bundled scraper in the option text (two includes relations, scoped to those Option values). Neither the store page nor the wiki gives an official packing list, so in_the_box stays empty and package.contents is not_published.

Adjudication against the second extraction: physical.thickness was not curated. The store cell publishes two layers ("Coating - 0.05mm / Steel Plate - 0.4mm") and the number key holds one; the deterministic page row keeps the cell as published (unverified), and a curated 0.4 mm at the same rank would not replace it, only mark a conflict between the page and itself. part.life_cycle stays the store's "consumable" sentence, not the marketing figure "less than 20% adhesion loss after 300 prints". Bambu PLA Silk is "not recommended", so it is neither in printing.unsupported_filament nor a not_compatible_with relation. safety.certifications is not listed as not_published: no plate-class file carries it and the sources give no certification for a build plate. part.color is not_published: neither wiki page nor the store page states the plate's colour. Packaging Size / Packaging Weight stay on the nine plate-only variants: the second extraction put the same segment figures on the Printer Model values, which would give the plate-only box to the "+ Mag-Alloy Scraper" bundles too. Printer targets follow compat-targets.json (P2S, H2D, A1, P1 Series and X1 Series are families there, not single printers). part.type (plates wiki, Build Plate Types list item 5) and package.contents as not_published (no packing list on the store page or either wiki page) are kept.
